title: Nicoise Salad
subtitle: tuna, egg, green beans, olives, and potato in a sharp vinaigrette
excerpt: Salade nicoise comes from Nice in the south of France and is built from the produce of that region -- tuna, olives, anchovy, and fresh vegetables. It is a substantial salad that works as a full meal. The components are prepared separately and arranged, never tossed.
sourceNotes: Salade nicoise originates from Nice in the Provence region of France. There is ongoing debate about the authentic version -- purists argue it should contain no cooked vegetables -- but the version with potato and green beans is widely accepted outside France.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook the potatoes and eggs up to a day ahead. Assemble just before serving.

content.text: Do not toss a nicoise. Arrange each component separately on the plate so the colours and textures stay distinct. The dressing goes on at the end.

items.prepNote: use 4 tuna steaks or 2 tins of good tuna in oil

content.text: Cook the potatoes in boiling salted water for 12 to 15 minutes until tender. Drain and cool.
Soft-boil the eggs for 7 minutes. Cool in cold water. Peel and halve.
Blanch the green beans for 3 minutes in boiling salted water. Drain and cool.
If using fresh tuna steaks, season and cook in a hot pan for 2 minutes each side. Leave to rest.
Arrange all the salad components on a large platter or individual plates. Drizzle the dressing over the top and serve.

items.fix: Cook tuna steaks for 2 minutes only each side. It should be pink in the centre.
Season the potatoes and beans while still warm. Cold vegetables do not absorb salt well.

content.text: Salade nicoise is one of the great dishes of Provencal cooking. It was eaten in Nice long before it became fashionable elsewhere. The purist version contains only raw vegetables -- tomato, pepper, celery, spring onion, anchovy, olive, and egg. The version with cooked potatoes and green beans is now accepted worldwide. Both have their place.
